about: Volter's year on X (journeys/customer-life.outline.md): Scheduler signed in with OAuth 1.0a, posting its devlog, a picture and a screen recording in chunks, reposting the devlog post once the audience likes it, refused the account's own posts for its analytics and reading one post's public metrics, publishing an Article; Dub's partner verifying her handle with OAuth 2.0 and PKCE; and the Model Editor's launch, posted by hand at x.com: Aaron signing in, posting the hero video and three pictures from the composer, watching the video play on the post's page, and a link whose card the post shows.

Model Editor by VideoGame AI
Your agent Fast Looks Made with it GitHub Install

Open source / Blender 5.2 / macOS on Apple Silicon

Real Blender.
Driven by your agent.

A model editor built on Blender 5.2, compiled to WebAssembly, with a viewport drawn in three.js and an interface you can restyle. The coding agent you already use does the modeling.

Install it See it work

Claude Code · Codex · Gemini · Grok · OpenRouter

Model
Script
Photograph
Save

01 / Your agent, at the controls

You ask.
Blender does it.

The Chat pane runs your coding agent beside Blender. It works through Blender's own Python: it builds, looks at what it made, fixes what it doesn't like, and saves to your .blend.

Ask
Build
Look
Fix

01 / 05

Claude Code replaces the starter cube with a desk lamp, photographs it, dims a blown-out light and shoots again. The middle runs at four times its speed.

Recorded in the editor, 0.5.79

02 / Light enough to stay interactive

Blender keeps the data.
three.js draws it.

Inside the editor Blender runs headless, as WebAssembly: every bpy call, modifier and save is Blender's own. The frames you see come from three.js over WebGL, so a whole game scene stays interactive.

Engine
Viewport
Interface

02 / 05

22msMedian frame
25ms95th percentile
5.8MTriangles in the scene

The Stoneguard Bridge scene below (3,467 meshes, 5.77 million triangles) in Material Preview: 60 frames drawn back to back and each waited out on the GPU, 2.9 million triangles drawn per frame, in a 1389 × 956 viewport. Measured on 0.5.94, in Chrome on a MacBook Pro with an M3 Pro.

03 / Make it yours

Five looks.
One file each.

The interface is React, so how it is drawn is a setting. Switch between the looks below: same scene, same panels. A script switches with editor.style("maya").

Blender
Maya
Substance
Glass
Classic

03 / 05

A look is data

A palette, a material and an icon set, contributed by a package. No code runs to load one.

{
  "name": "Maya",
  "theme": { "color": {
    "surface": { "panel": "#444444" },
    "accent":  { "default": "#5285a6" }
  } }
}

An editor is one call

The Model Editor's own entry picks Blender, the viewport, a look and a workspace from one kit.

product({
  id: 'model-editor',
  packages: { blender, threejs },
  look: 'blender',
  workspace: 'model',
});

04 / Made with it

One screenshot in.
A game's world out.

An agent was given one screenshot of a fantasy RPG and asked to rebuild it in Blender as a real, textured game scene. Working through Blender's MCP, it modeled the arched stone bridge, the river and its banks, the rocks and a mage on a fully rigged body. The Stoneguard Bridge game now plays in that scene.

Masonry
Terrain
Water
Characters

04 / 05

The game's own web scene, whole, open in the editor: 3,467 meshes and 5.8 million triangles. The mage stands in his rest pose; the exported scene carries no animation.

Actual capture

05 / Your agent, your account

Free to use.
Bring the agent you have.

The editor is open source and free to use. Your agent runs on your own account, so your model provider bills you directly; the editor adds no charge of its own.

Your keys
Your plan
Your files

05 / 05

Install

One command

Makes the project, installs the editor once and opens it. Runs on macOS with Apple Silicon and needs Node.js 24.

npx @volter/model-editor create my-models

Agents

The ones you already use

  • Claude Code, on your Claude plan
  • Codex, on your ChatGPT plan
  • Gemini and Grok
  • Any model through your OpenRouter key

A few good questions

The details
matter.

Is it really Blender?+

Yes: Blender 5.2 compiled to WebAssembly from its public source, running headless. Your scripts use the same bpy, and projects save as ordinary .blend files.

What runs on my machine?+

The command sets up a local session server that holds your project and a packaged Code-OSS workbench, and opens the editor. Blender runs inside the editor as WebAssembly; your agent runs on your machine under your own account.

Which systems does it run on?+

macOS on Apple Silicon only, with Node.js 24. Windows and Linux are not supported yet.

Does it render like Cycles?+

Not yet. The viewport and renders are drawn by three.js; rendering is not yet at parity with Blender's Cycles.

What is the license?+

The editor is under AGPL-3.0 and Blender under the GPL. Licenses and notices are in the repository.

Who makes it?+

VideoGame AI, an AI game studio. We work with game studios and publishers to build AI workflows on the technology we build, and the Model Editor is the open-source tool we have released. Its npm package is @volter/model-editor.

model?

body.title: How we compiled Blender to WebAssembly

blocks.text: The Model Editor's modeling engine is Blender itself. We compiled Blender 5.2 to WebAssembly, and this is how the pieces fit.
Blender 5.2 runs headless, compiled to WebAssembly; it holds the scene, and three.js draws what it holds.
The agent works through Blender's own Python
Agents already know bpy, so we gave them Blender rather than a new modeling API: the coding agent inspects the scene, edits it and photographs what it made.
Edits save to an ordinary .blend file and survive reopening.
